name: Oviedo front – Cerdeño bunker
story: Once the Galician relief column had reached Oviedo in October 1936, the Nationalist defenders ringed the city with concrete positions facing the Republican lines on Monte Naranco and in the surrounding villages. Archaeologists have mapped many trenches and bunkers around Oviedo. They remained on a front line until Asturias fell in October 1937. The concrete bunker at Cerdeño, on the northern edge of the city below the Naranco, is one of the surviving Nationalist works. Just above rise the slopes of Monte Naranco, fought over repeatedly during the siege and the February 1937 offensive.
see: A concrete Nationalist bunker on the northern outskirts of Oviedo.
plan: On the edge of the village of Cerdeño, north of the city centre. Access may be over farmland, so ask before crossing fields.
